title: Use NamedWritable to enable GeoBoundingBox serialisation

timeline.body:
`BoundingBox` allows inter-node serialisation only within aggs results as components of aggregations that themselves use `NamedWritable`. However, if a `GeoBoundingBox` is added to search `hits`, serialisation fails as this type is not explicitly supported by `StreamOuput/StreamInput`. This was never noticed before because the only way to get a `BoundingBox` into the `hits` is through a painless script, something that appears to have not been used by customers, and is only tested internally using a single-node, single-shard yaml test, which does not touch this code path. We only found this issue due to recent effort to run all yaml tests in a serverless environment, which appears to always require serialisation from backend data nodes to a coordinator node.

Having said that, it is a surface API that could be used by users, and so should be fixed. While the missing type could be added explicitly, a much more flexible approach is to allow named classes to encapsulate their own serialization/deserialization logic. Here we use `NamedWritable` for that purpose.

Tasks:

- [x] Implement GenericNamedWriteable with version checking capabilities (based on VersionedNamedWriteable)
- [x] Manual testing with a multi-node cluster to verify this fixes #99089
- [x] Unit tests for version checking
- [x] Unit tests for serialization of GeoBoundingBox
- [x] Support CartesianBoundingBox by registering the named writable in SpatialPlugin

Fixes #99089
Hi @craigtaverner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

This makes me a little uncomfortable, we should use a more precise class than just `NamedWriteable`. But I see why it's tricky here when we really don't know the context in which we're reading.

Could we introduce a marker type called `GenericNamedWriteable` and use that instead of `NamedWriteable`? That would help to protect against just accepting absolutely any `NamedWriteable` here.

Also I think this counts as a new transport version, we need to add a new version constant and throw an exception if the remote node version is too old rather than sending it something it won't understand.

reply.body: Great advice. I'm creating GenericNamedWriteable to extend VersionedNamedWriteable, which also provides the version checking.
I recommend not using `VersionNamedWriteable`, it is kind of a bad idea (it's designed to just silently drop stuff when sending to older versions, and that's almost certainly a mistake).
Actually wait, I see, it could be useful here. But we do need to throw something (and ideally `assert false` too) if the sender is trying to send a value that the receiver won't understand.

That code looks good, but does it really do anything different to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/io/stream/VersionCheckingStreamOutput.java#L64? That code should be called already, inside the call to `writeNamedWritable`, so the check already exists, as far as I can tell.

What I would like would be compatibility checks that verify that the exception is indeed thrown when we have mix-clusters. I wrote some tests like this before (in other work), but they were flaky (throwing the expected exception 99% of the time, not 100%, which was odd). I can try again.

`VersionCheckingStreamOutput` doesn't consider it a bug to try and send an unknown writable, it just throws an IAE which maps onto a `400 Bad Request` and isn't logged. I think that's unduly lenient (although I see why checking this properly is tricky in a cross-cluster situation) and I'd rather we were stricter where possible, asserting that this doesn't happen and throwing an ISE if ever it does.

> What I would like would be compatibility checks that verify that the exception is indeed thrown when we have mix-clusters.

I think a unit test is enough for this. We shouldn't even be trying to send unknown stuff over the wire ideally, hence why I think we should assert that we don't. Instead I'd rather that we looked at `org.elasticsearch.cluster.ClusterState#getMinTransportVersion` and avoided even creating the problematic object until all nodes can understand it.

I'm thinking, if we have a mixed cluster, and there is a query involving a new feature that requires sending something new over the wire, that only some of the cluster understands, the consequence is:

* If the sender is an old version, it will not even get to this point because the new feature is not understood causing an exception in the feature itself (eg. in my case the painless script will fail with a painless exception).
* If the sender is new, but the receiver is old, then the sender serialises type=30, and the receiver throws `IOException("Can't read unknown type [" + type + "]")` in `StreamInput.readGenericValue`.

So, as far as I can tell your suggestion is that instead of the receiver throwing this exception, we have a sender that detects the receiver is old and throws an exception before sending, which moves the error to a different node in the cluster. Is this a big improvement?

In fact there are three scenarios:

* If we do no checking of versions at all (ie. my initial code) we get the behaviour described above
* If we check with VersionedNamedWritable (ie. my current code) we get an exception in the sender if the VersionedNamedWritable version is later than the senders TransportVersion which only considers local node state, so does not care if the remote node has an older version
* We check the remote transport version also, and throw an exception there. Looking at your code, it does not do this but seems to consider local transport version only, so very similar to the current behaviour. Perhaps your last suggestion of using `ClusterState#getMinTransportVersion` is the way to do this? But again, the consequence is only to move the exception to a different node in the cluster.

I've done a little more digging and it looks like VersionedNamedWritable checks only occur for CCS, way too narrow a scope for our needs, so it is clear that I do need to write the check you have suggested. I'll go for that now.

We should forbid the use of any features that the whole cluster does not understand (which is why I think we should be looking at `ClusterState#getMinTransportVersion`). At least, that's [the documented behaviour](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elastic-stack/8.9/upgrading-elasticsearch.html#rolling-upgrades). Then we should consider it a bug (and `assert false`) if ever we get into a position where we're trying to send a message that the remote won't understand.

> Looking at your code, it does not do this but seems to consider local transport version only

No, it's looking at `StreamOutput#getTransportVersion` which is a transport version compatible with both sender and receiver.
I've investigated further and figured out why I misunderstood this. I did not see the uses of `setTransportVersion`, which allows for the behaviour you describe.

timeline.body:
I think it'd be better to have this in the concrete subclasses. That way if we add another one in future we won't forget to set this to the correct value.

Also it (and the `getWriteableName` implementations) probably should to be `final` to make sure we don't accidentally add further subclasses without thinking about the consequences in this area..

reply.body: Done

timeline.body: This will always return the value of `genericNamedWriteable.getMinimalSupportedVersion()` since the concept of `GenericNamedWritable` was only introduced at this version.

reply.body:
That's true, as long `getMinimalSupportedVersion()` is implemented correctly and not (say) copied from one of the implementations that returns `TransportVersion.MINIMUM_COMPATIBLE`. However BwC serialization is fairly subtle, and bugs in this area are just awful, so I'd like the extra check.

(We could also reasonably assert that `genericNamedWriteable.getMinimalSupportedVersion().onOrAfter(V_8_500_069)`)
I've added the assert now

timeline.body: These asserts seem to cause integration tests to fail in more opaque ways, with the test code receiving less information about the failure. Is this generally a good idea? Is the advantage that we fail faster, and so avoid being mislead by later errors?

reply.body: We definitely want to fail here in tests, and simply throwing an exception won't necessarily do that because exceptions can be caught. It's unfortunate that we have less context to share here, although I would expect these things to be fairly easy to reproduce.
At least here we assert with the same message. The test failure I debugged recently failed without the message, hiding the reason for failure, making it much harder to track initially.

timeline.message:
Use GenericNamedWriteable to limit this to specific classes

So only classes that implement this specific interface will benefit from this additional capability.
Also we implement VersionedNamedWriteable to ensure that TransportVersion checking is done.
timeline.author: Craig Taverner

+ * generic serialization in StreamOutput and StreamInput.
+ */
+public interface GenericNamedWriteable extends VersionedNamedWriteable {

timeline.message:
Ensure serialization tests use the generic code path

The parent class AbstractNamedWriteableTestCase was not using the writeGenericValue and readGenericValue that this work changed, so we override that behaviour to ensure we're testing the new code.

We also add a new test method for negative testing of errors thrown when trying to serialize using an older TransportVersion.
We do not throw similar errors on reading, with the assumption that the reader can always read things it knows about, regardless of the age of the sender.
Taking account the TransportVersion in the reader only make sense if reading a known type where the format has changed.
timeline.author: Craig Taverner

timeline.message:
Support CartesianBoundingBox in StreamOutput/Input

This is one reason why we went for a generic approach, allowing plugins to register additional GenericNamedWriteables that can be serialized/deserialized by the StreamInput/StreamOutput code without the server depending on xpack.
